translations.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. This man was upright, pure, and righteous, and he feared God. He kept himself wholeheartedly away from every evil deed.
He had seven sons and three daughters.
His livestock numbered seven hundred; his sheep, three thousand; his camels, five hundred; his teams of cattle, five hundred; and his female donkeys, five hundred.
He had very many servants, and his work on the earth was great. He was a good man in the land of the dawn, where the sun rises.
His sons would go and gather together and hold a feast every day. They would bring their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

When the days of their feasting were over, Job would send them before God and seek forgiveness for them. He would rise early in the morning and offer sacrifices on their behalf, according to their number.
And one bull for the sin of his own soul.
Job would say, “Perhaps my children have thought something evil against God.” Job did this throughout all the days of his life.

After that day, the angels of God came, and Satan also came with them and stood in his place. 10. God said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered God and said to him, “I have traveled around the whole earth and wandered beneath heaven, and I have come.”

God said to Satan, “Surely you have nothing to devise against my [?] Job, for there is no one like him on earth: a pure and righteous man who fears God and keeps himself wholeheartedly away from every evil deed.”

Satan answered before God and said, “Does Job [?] worship God for nothing? And everything around him [?]. You have blessed the work of his hands and multiplied his livestock on the earth. Are you not [?] for him, inside and outside his house?”
“But stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and see whether he does not curse you to your face!”
Then God said to Satan, “Look, I have put everything he has into your hand. But do not strike him himself.” Satan went out from God's presence rejoicing.
On that day, Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking in their eldest brother's house.
A messenger came to Job and said to him, “Your teams of cattle were plowing, and your female donkeys were grazing nearby.
“Raiders came and carried them off, and they killed your servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”

While he was reporting this to Job, another messenger came and said to Job, “Fire fell from heaven and burned your sheep and consumed your shepherds along with them. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”

While he was reporting this to Job, a third messenger came and said to Job, “Men mounted on horses and three large bands intercepted and carried off your camels and cattle, and they killed your servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”

While he was telling him this, a fourth messenger came and said to Job, “While your sons and daughters were eating and drinking in their eldest brother's house, a great wind suddenly came from the wilderness and struck the house at its four corners.”
The house fell on your sons and daughters, and they died. I alone escaped and came to tell you.

Then, when Job heard this news, he rose, tore his clothes, shaved the hair of his head, fell to the ground, and worshiped. 23. He said, “Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked I will return to the earth. God gave, and God took away. It happened as God wished. Nevertheless, blessed be the name of God.”
Then, after that day, the angels of God came and stood before God. Satan also came with them and stood before him.
God said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan said before God, “I went beneath heaven and wandered everywhere, and I have come.”

God said to Satan, “Surely you have devised nothing like this against my servant Job, for there is no one like him on earth: an innocent, righteous, good, and pure man who fears God and keeps himself wholeheartedly away from every wicked deed. He is still innocent, yet you said to destroy his possessions for no reason.”
Satan answered God and said, “Skin for skin! A person will give everything he owns in exchange for his life.”

But stretch out your hand and strike his bones and his flesh, and see whether he will not curse you to your face. 6. The Lord said to Satan, “Look, I have given his flesh and his bones into your hand, but spare his life.” 7. Satan went out from the Lord’s presence rejoicing, and afflicted Job with terrible sores from his feet to his head.

He took a potsherd and began scraping his sores. He stayed outside the city and lay in dirt and dust. 9. After many days had passed, his wife said to Job, “How long will you endure in innocence? Curse God and die! Are you still saying, ‘I will wait for God a few more days; I will continue to endure and hope for my former life’?”
“Look, your memory has vanished from the earth. My sons and daughters have died. My womb suffered with painful anguish; I labored and toiled for nothing.”

You sit amid pus and worms and spend the whole night in the open, while I wander and roam, going from place to place and from house to house. I wait from dawn until sunset to find relief from my toil and from the suffering that weighs upon me. But now speak a word against God and die.” 12. Job looked at her and said to her, “You have spoken like one of the foolish women. We have received good from the hand of God; should we not, then, endure evil?” In all that befell him, Job committed no sin against God.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day on which he was born.
He said, “Let the day on which I was born perish, and the night on which they said, ‘It is a boy.’
Let that day become dark. Let God above take no notice of it, and let no light come into it.
Let darkness seize it, and let the shadow of death cover it. Let a dark cloud come upon it; let that day be cursed.
Let darkness come upon that night. Let it have no place among the days of the year, and let it not be counted among the days of the months.
Let anguish overtake that day, and let neither joy nor gladness enter it.
Rather, let the one who cursed that day curse it, the one who is to cut apart the great sea monster.
Let the stars of that night grow dark, and let them remain where they see no light.
Because they did not close the door of my mother’s womb, and did not see [?] as it rose, and did not remove suffering from my eyes.
Why did I not die in the womb? Why, when I came out of the womb, did I not perish immediately?
Why did my knees grow strong, and why was I cradled at the breast?
Had I lain down then, I would now be silent; had I fallen asleep then, I would now be at rest,
with kings who plotted evil upon the earth and passed judgment with the sword,
or with messengers and wealthy men who accumulated gold and filled their houses with silver.
Or if only I had been like a miscarried child expelled from its mother’s womb.
There sinners cease their terror, and they burn under the scourge of his wrath.
There those whose bodies have been confined also rest together from [?] the toil of the world.
There are the small and the great. Infants who have seen no light and have not heard the voice of the taskmaster are there. The servant who served his master is also there.
Why have you given light to the embittered, and life to those blind in soul?
They long for death but do not find it, and they fear it like a buried treasure and rejoice if they [?] it. Death is rest for a human being, and God [?] it from his mouth.
After my harvest, my scourge overtook me.
I weep because of the terror that has overtaken me. A fear I did not anticipate has overtaken me, and what I did not imagine has assailed me.”
I had no quiet, no rest, and no safety, and scourging and suffering came upon me.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite spoke in reply:
He said, “Do not speak at length while you are suffering. What good will multiplying words do you?”
“You used to instruct many and encourage weary hands.
You used to raise up the sick with your words and strengthen feeble knees.
But now that suffering has come upon you and rebuked you, you yourself are distressed; you have [?], then.
From the beginning, was not your fear foolishness, and your hope and your path evil?
Remember that no innocent person has been destroyed, and the righteous do not perish or get uprooted.
As we have seen, those who plow sin and sow it reap scourges for themselves.
They perish at God's command and waste away under the scourge of his wrath.
The lion’s roar, the lioness’s cry, and the young lions’ majesty have perished.

The old lion too perished for lack of food, and the lion cubs perished among themselves. 12. But if you had done even one righteous deed, all this would not have surrounded you. A word arose near me, and my ear heard a sound from it. At first I did not believe the one who told me.
The terror of night and deep sleep come suddenly upon a person.
Fear covered me; terror and trembling seized me, and [?] my bones.
My spirit passed before my face and made the hair of my head and body stand on end.
I arose and did not recognize you. I looked at you and could not make you out. You had no visible form before my eyes, but I see your shadow and hear your voice.
But who among mortals is pure before God, and what person is righteous in his deeds?
He does not trust his servants at all, and he finds fault even with his angels.
As for those who dwell in houses of earth—and we too are from a single lump—worms overtake them and devour them, and they give no thought to it from morning until evening.
They do not survive from morning until evening. Because they cannot save or help themselves, they are destroyed.
The wind blows upon them, and they dry up and perish, because they have no wisdom.
Call now, and see whether anyone will answer you, and whether you will see any of his holy angels.
For wrath kills the fool, and the foolish person dies of jealousy.
I have seen the roots of fools sprout, but at once their dwelling perished, and they departed from life.
Their children too are beaten at the gates and abused, and there is no one to save them.
The righteous eat what they have gathered, but evil assails them, and their strength is drained away.
For toil does not come out of the earth, nor does suffering sprout from the mountains.
But people are born to work, and young birds soar in flight.
But I will ask God and call upon the Lord of all, who has done great things beyond counting, glorious and wonderful things that cannot be traced.
And he has done wonders beyond counting.
He gives rain upon the earth and sends water beneath heaven.
He raises the lowly and lifts up the outcast.
He overturns the plans of those who act cunningly, and their hands accomplish nothing right.
He catches the wise in their own counsel and destroys the plans of those who weave schemes.
Darkness meets them in the daytime. At noon they grope like a blind person, as though it were night, and they are destroyed in slaughter.
He rescues the weak from the hand of [?] the strong, giving hope to [?], and the oppressor’s mouth is shut.
But blessed is the person whom God corrects. Do not despise God's discipline.
For he wounds and heals again; he strikes, and his hands show mercy.
He will rescue you from six troubles, and in the seventh no evil will touch you.
In famine he will save you from death, and in war he will rescue you from the power of the sword.
He will hide you from the scourge of the tongue, and you will not fear the evil that comes.
You will laugh at sinners and violent people. You will not fear the beasts of the field, and the beasts of the wilderness will be at peace with you.
Then you will know that your house is safe and that nothing is missing from your possessions.
You will know that your offspring are numerous, and your children are like the flourishing grass of the ground.
You will enter your grave like ripe grain at harvest, and like a heap from which people take at every season.
Look, this is the trail we have traced, and this is what we have heard. But you yourself must know what you have done.
Then Job answered in this way and said:
If only one of you would weigh my affliction and lift it together with my suffering on a balance! For it is heavier than the sand of the sea.
Yet my truthful words seem false. Look, God's arrows are in my flesh, and their poison drains my blood. When I begin to speak, they pierce my flesh.
Does a wild donkey bray for nothing among the green plants? Is it not seeking something to eat? Does an ox bellow while it is eating and feeding at the manger?
Can food be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the juice of the plant called marshmallow? Is there any taste in empty words?
My soul cannot rest, and I see the [?] of my flesh, like the stench of a lion. 7. If only my prayer would be answered and God would grant me my hope!
God took hold of me, finished me off, and killed me forever.
When [?], and I return to his rest, let him not spare me, for I have not denied the word of my holy God.
What strength do I have, that I should endure? How many days do I have, that my soul should submit?
Is my flesh bronze? Or is my strength the strength of stone?
Was it not in him that I trusted? Why, then, has his help gone far from me?
His mercy has rejected me. God has not looked upon me or sheltered me with his mercy.
My relatives have not acknowledged me, like a stream that has dried up and like a wave that has passed away. Those who fear me are the very ones who laugh at me.
Like hail and frost that has frozen solid, which then melted in the heat, and the place where it had been was no longer known.
In the same way, I too have gone away from everything and have perished; I have gone out of my house.
You know the journeys of the people of Tema, and the misfortune of the people of Sheba and their wanderings.
Truly, those who trust in their possessions and in their houses will be put to shame.
So you too have come without mercy. You saw my wound and were not afraid. Why?
Have I asked anything of you? Or have I desired your strength, that you should save me from my enemy and rescue me from the hand of the one who overpowers me?
Teach me, teach me, and I will be silent. If I have gone wrong in anything, make it clear to me, for my truthful words seem false.
It is not from you that I ask for strength and comfort. Your words will not lead me astray, nor will the clamor of your words bewilder me, for you have laughed at your friend and mocked a mortal man.
Now, as I look at your faces, I will not lie to you. Sit down, but do not act unjustly, and speak rightly once again.
For there is no unjust word on my tongue, and my throat speaks wisdom.
First, is not human life on earth a shadow, and human existence like a daily thought?
And is it not like a servant who pleases his master and longs for shade, or like a hired worker who hopes for his wages?
Likewise, I too have endured empty months, and nights of suffering have been given to me.
When I sleep, I say, “When will morning come for me?” And when I wake, I say again, “When will evening come?”
I was filled with pain from morning until evening. My flesh swelled with [?] and pus, and they wore away as I scratched. I became [?], [?], and dust.
My life became fleeting, like something dreamed, and I perished with an empty hope.
Remember that my life is a breath, and my eye will never again see anything good. 8. The eye of the one who sees me will no longer see me; even if he looks for me, I will no longer be there.
Like a cloud cleared away from the sky, a person who has gone down into the grave will not come up again.
He will not return to his house, and his place will no longer know him.
Because of this, I too will not keep my mouth silent. I will speak of the suffering of my spirit and reveal the bitterness of my soul that weighs upon me, for my tears have become a sea.
Am I a sea or a deep, that you have appointed a guard over me?
I said, ‘Surely my bed will comfort me, and surely my couch will give me relief.’
But you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
He gained power over my soul and my spirit, and [?] my eyes. Will I live forever, so that I should endure? Go far away from me, for my life is empty.
What is a human being, that you exalt him and keep watch over his heart?
Or that you test him until he comes to you, or judge him on his bed?
How long will you refuse to leave me alone, even long enough for me to swallow my saliva while it chokes me?

Even if I have sinned, what then can I do to you, you who know the human heart? Why have you appointed me to receive your scourging, and why did you create me in your likeness? Yet I have become a burden to you.
Why have you not made my sin forgotten and my wrongdoing cleansed? Now I will descend into the earth, where no one wakes again.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long will you speak like this? Is there a spirit of speech in your mouth?
Does God judge unjustly? Does the Creator of all trouble the righteous?
If your children sinned before him, he sent them away because of their sin.
But you, go to God and pray.
If you are righteous and pure, he will quickly hear your prayer and reward you for your righteousness.
Even if your beginning is small, your latter state will be beyond counting.
Job says this: ‘Can I ascend to heaven and steal its treasures, and plumb the depths of the earth?’ Likewise, ask those of ancient times, and question the fathers in their respective clans.
We are only of yesterday and know nothing, and our life on earth is a shadow.
They will teach you and tell you, and bring forth words for you from their hearts.
Can grass sprout without water, or can greenery grow without being watered? 12. All grass that does not drink water dries up before it is cut.
Such is the end of all who forget God, and the hope of sinners will perish.
It is ruined, and his dwelling will become a spider’s web.
Even if he strengthens his house, it will not stand; what he has begun he will not complete.
His house is [?] beneath the sun, and the greenery in his garden dries up.
His strength is exhausted through his wickedness. He spends the night among rocks and lives among gravel.
And if the earth swallows him and denies him, saying, “I have never seen such a thing,” the wicked will likewise be overthrown.
And another will sprout from the earth.
But God will not abandon the innocent or strengthen the hands of evildoers, nor will he accept the offering of sinners.
He will fill the mouths of the upright with laughter, and their lips will give thanks.
Their enemies will be clothed with shame, and the house of sinners will perish.
And Job spoke in reply and said:
Truly, I know that this is so. But how can a righteous person be pure before God?
Even if he wished to dispute with him, he could not answer him one word out of a thousand.
He is wise in counsel and great in strength. Who has acted wickedly and stood before him?
He shakes the mountains, though they do not see him, and overturns them in his wrath.
He shakes the earth from its foundations.
He shakes the pillars of heaven and darkens its stars.
He walks upon the sea as upon the earth, and he alone spread out the heavens.
He says to the moon, “Do not rise,” and seals up the faces of the stars. He made the Pleiades and gathered them together, and Aldebaran too, and he counts the morning stars.
He makes many things and gathers them together; he sees and counts the nations. He has done great things beyond number.
If he passes by me, I do not see him; if he goes past, I do not recognize him.
And if he takes something away, who will bring it back? Who will say to him, “What have you done?”
God has not turned away from scourging me, and the leopards beneath heaven have been chastised by him.
How, then, will he hear my words and consider them?
Even if I call out in righteousness and he does not hear me, I will ask for his judgment.
Even if I called out in righteousness and he answered me, I would not believe that he had heard me.
His whirlwind crushes me, and he has wounded me greatly without cause.
He has not let me rest, and he has filled me with bitterness.
For he takes hold firmly, and who can oppose his judgment? Even if my mouth departed from righteousness, and even if I fell short of righteousness, something dreadful would come upon me.
I am innocent, yet I do not know myself; nevertheless, my life has perished.

But I said, “The great and mighty one sends a scourge, for the death of sinners is evil. They mock the righteous, and the righteous fall into the hands of sinners. They cover the faces of the judges. And I—what am I?”
My life passes more swiftly than runners who rush away and cannot now be caught.
And even if there is a ship, the trace of its path cannot be recognized, or an eagle flying and searching for something to eat.
Even if I spoke, it would do no good. My face fell as I cried out, and all my limbs trembled. Then I knew that he would not leave me as I was.
If I am a sinner, why did I not die?
Even if I washed myself and became clean as snow, and thoroughly cleansed my hands,
you would plunge me into filth, and my own clothing would abhor me.
If the one who contends with me were a man, we would go together into court.
Would that there were a chosen person to judge between us and hear both of us, and that this rod were taken away from me.
If his terror did not assail me, I would speak to him, though I do not see him.
Then I would speak, and he would not be afraid.
I know nothing while my soul suffers. In exhaustion I utter my words, and I speak while my soul is crushed with bitterness.
I say to God, “Will you not forgive sin? Why have you condemned me this way?”
Does it seem good to you if I do wrong, since you have rejected the work of your hands and looked upon the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have human eyes? Do you look and see as a mortal does?
Are your days like human days, and your years like those of a mortal, that you search for sin and investigate my wrongdoing?
You know that I have not sinned against you, yet who can rescue me from your hand?
Your hands formed me and made me, and afterward you cast me away and cleansed me.
Remember that you formed me from clay, and you will return me again to the earth.
You drew me out like milk and curdled me like cheese.
You clothed me with flesh and skin, and bound my bones together with sinews.
You gave me kindness, mercy, and life, and your care preserved my spirit.
All this is with you. I know that you can do everything and that nothing is beyond your power.
If I sinned, you would have guarded me and cleansed me from my sin.
And when I sinned, woe to me [?]! And when they acted righteously [?], I could not lift it up, and I was filled with disgrace.
I became like a lion that is trapped and killed, without [?]. Again you bring me to death and utterly torment me.
Once again you question me from the beginning. You have brought a great scourge upon me and sent trials against me.
Why, then, did I not die when you brought me out of my mother’s womb, so that no eye would have seen me and I would have been as though I had never been created?
Why was I created, instead of going down to the grave? Why, when I came out of the womb, was I not destroyed at once?
Why did I not rest in the grave? Are not the days of my life few, and my months numbered?

Leave me alone so that I may rest a little before I go where there is no return, to a land of darkness and gloom, a land of everlasting darkness where there is no light, and where the dead see neither light nor life.
Then Zophar the Ammonite spoke in reply and said:
The more you speak, the further you sink. Do you think you are justified by an abundance of empty words?
Blessed is the one born of women, whose days are few. Do not multiply your words.
Do not say, “I am pure in my deeds, and I am righteous before him.”

If only God would speak to you and open his lips to you! He would tell you the power of wisdom, for what confronts you is astonishing. 7. Then you would know that what you have received from God is what you deserved for your sins. Can you find God's tracks? Were you there before him, at the beginning, when he created the whole world and the high heavens?
What can you do, and what do you know of the depth of the abyss?
And the height of heaven, and the width of the earth, or the breadth of the sea.

If he overturns everything, who will say to him, “What have you done?” 11. He himself knows the deeds of sinners, and if he sees wrongdoing, he will not remain silent. And [?], and a wise man will instruct him.
For a man, he is a seeker of words; and a mortal born of women seems to me like a donkey. 13. But you say, “My heart is pure,” and raise your hands toward me.
But when there is no wrongdoing in your hands, and if you have not lodged hatred in your heart, then your face will shine like that of someone washed with clean water.
And you will be [?], and [?] impurity, and you will no longer be afraid.

You will forget your suffering like a wave that has passed, and you will no longer weep. Your prayer will be like the morning star, and your life will rise like daylight. 17. You will be confident that you will find [?], and you will live at ease, without sorrow or distress.
Then you will rest, and there will be no one to attack you. Many will come and praise you.
But the deliverance of sinners will come to an end, and they will lose their hope, and the eyes of the wicked will fail.
Then Job spoke in reply and said:
Are you, then, the people, and has wisdom indeed taken power among you?
I too have understanding like you, for there is no one like God. He becomes a laughingstock to his neighbor, and the righteous, innocent man is a laughingstock.
A righteous and pure man became an object of mockery throughout the days of his life.
They kept him waiting for strangers to defile him and to bring down the house of sinners.
Yet the wicked who provoke God say, “We are good.” Is he not the one who calls them to account?
Ask the animals whether they will tell you, and the birds of the sky whether they will teach you.
Speak to the earth, and perhaps it will teach you; perhaps the fish of the sea will tell you.
Who knows that the hand of the Lord has made all this?
For in his hand are the life of every living thing and the breath of every human being.
Does not the ear distinguish words, and the palate taste food?
Is wisdom found in many years, and learning in a long lifetime?
But all wisdom and power come from God, and counsel and understanding belong to him.
If he tears down, who will build? And if he shuts someone in, who will open? 15. If he withholds rain from heaven, he dries up the earth; and if he releases it, the earth is ruined and overturned.
For strength and might come from me, and wisdom and counsel belong to him.
He makes counselors captives and carries off the rulers of the earth.
He seats kings on thrones and fastens a belt of strength around their waists.
He sends priests away as captives and overthrows the mighty of the earth.
He changes the speech of the faithful and knows the counsel of the learned.
He brings disgrace upon rulers and shows mercy to the humble.
He reveals deep things out of darkness and brings them into the light out of darkness and the shadow of death.
He throws nations into confusion, and they perish; he sets nations in order and guides them.
He changes the counsel of the rulers of the earth and makes them wander on a road they do not know.
Look, this is what my eye has seen and my ear has heard.
I know what you know, and I am no more foolish than you.
But I will speak to God and argue before him, if he wishes. 4. But you are all keepers of wrongful remedies and comforters of evil.
Your silence does not set me right, for wisdom has vanished from you.
Listen to the rebuke from my mouth, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
And now, are you not sitting before God and uttering [?] before him and shrinking back from him? Come, judge for yourselves.
Is it good if they question you while you do everything? Seek him.
To what will you compare him, so that you can argue with him? You show favoritism [?] and hide deceit from him.
Will his power not frighten you in his presence, and will terror not come upon you from him?
Your reproach passes away like dust, and your flesh is earth.
Be silent before me so that I may speak and find relief from anger.
I have gathered my flesh between my teeth and placed my life in my hands.
I will snatch my garment away from [?]. And if I have not snatched it away by force, if it has not been taken away [?]. Otherwise, I will speak and argue before him.
This will become my salvation, for deceit will not enter his presence.
Listen to my words, and I will tell you while you listen to me.
Look, I have come to present my case, and I know that my innocence will be revealed.
And who is it who has been confined, so that I should now be silent and keep still? I will become like a fool. Shall I hide from your face?
Withdraw your hand from me, and do not let your majesty terrify me. 20. You will call me, and I will listen to you; and if you speak to me, I too will answer you.
How many are my sins and my offenses? Show me what they are.
Why do you hide from me and regard me as your enemy?
You harass me like a leaf shaken by the wind, and you shake me like grass carried away by the wind. You pursue dry grass and [?].
For you have written down my evil deeds against me [?], and you have kept the sins of my youth against me. You have confined me and put my feet in the stocks [?].
You have set my deeds before yourself [?], and when my foot stood firm, you abandoned me.
A mortal born of woman has few days and is full of the affliction of wrath.
He blossoms like a flower and falls; he passes like a shadow and no longer remains.
Yet you have called even this man to account and brought him into judgment with you.
Who can be clean from impurity? No one, even if he has lived only one hour on earth. 5 For the number of his months is with you; you give him his allotted lifetime, and he cannot go beyond it.
Turn away from him so that he may rest and wait out his life like a hired worker.
For a tree has hope: when it is cut down, it will bear fruit again and put out shoots, and its strength will not fail.
Even if its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies among the rocks, at the scent of water it will put out shoots and bear fruit like a new plant.
When a man dies, he passes away; when a mortal dies, he no longer exists. 10. Even the sea has hope when it receives water, but a river dwindles and dries up.
But once a man has fallen asleep, he does not wake again until heaven passes away, and they awaken from their sleep.
It would have been better for me if you had kept me in the grave and hidden me [?] until [?] your wrath cooled, and kept me until the time when you remembered me.
If a man could live after he had died, I would endure all the days of my life until I was born again.
I would answer when you called me, and you would not reject me, the work of your hands. 15 You have counted my sins and my offenses together, and you have forgotten none of my sins or offenses.
You have sealed up my errors in your bag, and everything in which I have sinned against you.
Like a mountain that collapses and falls, a rock too wears away where it stands.

Stone is worn smooth by water, and water is buried within the earth, Most High. You have destroyed a person's endurance. 19 You overpower him forever, and he passes away [?]. You turn your face toward him and carry him away.
Even if his children become numerous [?], he does not see them; and if they are few, he does not know them.
But his flesh wastes away, and his soul [?] for life.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite spoke and said:
First, does a wise man answer with thoughts of wind [?]? You have filled our soul and our body with [?].
You argue with empty words and speak what is of no use. 4 Did you yourself not fear him, that you should speak such words before God?
Your measure is not from the words of your mouth [?], and you have not discerned the speech of the great.
The words of your own mouth condemn you, not I, and your lips testify against you.
Were you created before other human beings, or were you established before the hills?
Have you heard God's command, and has wisdom been stored up with you? 9. What do you know that we do not know, and what do you understand that we do not understand?
Young men and elders are among us, including one older than your father.
Although you have been punished for only a few of your sins, what you have said is beyond what is fitting for you.
Why, then, has your heart gone mad, so that you speak angrily before God and pour such words out of your mouth? And what have your eyes seen?
What mortal is clean from sin, and who born of women is righteous?

Let alone an unclean and filthy person who drinks down sin! He puts no trust at all in the holy ones, and even heaven is not clean before him. 15. Listen to me, and I will tell you; I will explain to you what I have seen, and what the wise have told and their fathers did not hide from their children. For the land was given to them alone, and no other people passed among them.
The sinner suffers torment all his days, and his days and years are allotted to him by number.
Terror brings down the mighty. When he hopes to live safely, he is plundered. 18. He has no hope of coming out of darkness; he has already been appointed for the hand of the sword.
He is given as food to vultures, and he himself does not know that a sudden blow and darkness await him.

Suffering and poverty drive him from his house, like a messenger appointed to go ahead, and he is put to shame, because he raised his hand against God and stiffened his neck before God, who rules everything. 21. His disgrace terrifies him, and in his prosperous days his strength [?].

Death covers him as he passes and waits for him behind his back. He lives in ruined cities and spends the night in a plundered house; what he prepared, another will take away. 23. Even if he becomes rich, his wealth will not endure, and he will cast no shadow over the earth.
He will not escape from darkness. The wind will dry up his roots, and his fruit will fall.
He will not hope to live, and what he hoped for will disappoint him, and he will fall. 26. His unripe grapes will be consumed, and he will fall like the fruit of an olive tree.
The verdict on sinners is death. Fire will burn the house of those who take gifts unjustly. 28. In their wombs they conceive trouble, and their wombs bring forth deceit.
Then Job spoke in reply and said:
I have heard many things like these. All of you are comforters who bring harm. 3. You speak whatever comes to you, without restraint. How have I troubled you, that you answer me this way?
I too could answer you as you speak. Would your souls be [?] in place of my soul?
I would speak words to you and shake my head at you.
If only I then had strength in my mouth, I would not hold back my lips, and I would seek what to say.
Even if I speak, my wound does not heal; and if I remain silent, my suffering grows worse.
But now you have made me a shattered fool, a broken fragment.
Your seizure of me has become a witness, and my falsehood has risen against me and accused me to my face.
Enraged in his anger, he assailed me and ground his teeth against me; my [?] plotted against me. 11. They struck my eyes, and he alone threw me down onto my knees, and together they rushed at me.
He handed me over to one who torments me, and God cast me into the hands of the wicked.
While I was living safely, he cast me down and seized me by the hair at the back of my neck. He set me up like a target and like a bow, and watched me closely like the pupil of an eye.
For they struck me with arrows and pierced my kidneys, and they had no mercy on me. My gall was poured out onto the ground.
Disaster upon disaster overtook me, and mighty men rushed against me.
They fastened sackcloth over my skin, and my suffering grew stronger in the earth.
My belly burns from weeping, and I see the shadow of death upon my eyelids.
There is no injustice in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
Will the earth cover my flesh, and will my blood be poured out? Will there be no place where I can cry out?
Even now, look: my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.
My prayer has reached God, and my eyes shed tears before him.
When they plead a man's case with God, as a human being with his neighbor, empty years will come upon me.
And I will go along a road from which no one returns.
What burns my soul wears me down. I long for the grave, but it is of no avail.
I have labored while pleading; what shall I do? Strangers strip me of my possessions.
And who is it that will turn my hand back?
For they hid their plunder from what is good, and because of this he will not exalt them.
They teach their hearts evil, and my eyes waste away because of my children.
You have made me a subject of talk among the nations, and I have become an object of laughter and mockery to them.
My eyes have gone blind from tears, and they have all made me shudder even more.
I trusted in this, but it made me despair; yet it rightly comes upon sinners.
Nevertheless, I trust that I will return along my way. Because my hands are pure, I will find my joy.
All of you must look at me and come here, for I find no upright person among you.
My days have come to an end, defiled, and the root of my heart has been cut off.
Day has become night for me, and darkness has come upon me in the presence of light.
Even if I linger, my home is in the grave, and my bed has been spread in darkness.
I call death my father, and worms are my mother and my brothers.
Where, then, is my hope? Will I see anything good?
Will it descend into the grave with me, and will we be buried together in the earth?
Bildad spoke again and answered. 2. He said, "How long will you refuse to be silent? Restrain yourself now, so that we too may speak to you."
Why have we fallen silent before you like animals?
It is fitting for your punishment. And what are you at the time of your death? Is there no one better under heaven? Will the mountains fall from their foundations?
The light of sinners will perish, and their wickedness will not be concealed.
Their light will become darkness for them. They will go astray, and their lamp will go out.
The lowly will take his possessions, and his plans will fail.
His foot will descend into a trap and be caught in a snare.
Punishment will come upon him, and mighty men will come against him.
His cord is hidden in the ground, and they will drag him from his path.
Disease will destroy him on every side, and many will come beneath his feet in great hunger.
Severe disgrace is waiting for him.
The joints of his feet will be gnawed away, and death will consume his beauty.
Sores break out from his flesh, his misery grows, and God takes vengeance on him.
He will be shut up in his house at night, and his Creator will scatter his beauty.
His roots dry up beneath him, and his fruit falls from above him.
His memory will perish from the earth, and his name will be removed far away.
They will drive him from light into darkness, and no one among his people will have mercy on him.
His household will not survive under heaven, and a stranger will take a share of his possessions.
The poor cried out because of him, and even the great were astonished at him.
Such is the fate of those who do not know God.
Then Job spoke in reply.
He said, “How long will you oppress my soul and harass me over my words?
But know that God has made me like this. Ten times you have spoken against me, and you are not ashamed to stand against my soul.
Yes, indeed, I went astray, and folly lodged with me. I spoke a word I did not understand; my speech too was foolish and not [?].
Woe to me! Yet you open your mouths wide against me, troubling me; you mock me and revile me.
But know that it is God who has troubled me and poured out his wrath upon me.
Look, I cry out against violence; I speak and lament, but there is no one to give me justice.
He has fenced me in on every side, and I have no way through. He has spread darkness before my face.
He has stripped me of my adornment, and I have no crown upon my head.
He has destroyed me on every side, and I am gone; he has cut down my life like a tree.
He has subjected me to a mighty scourge and treated me as an enemy.
His wrath came upon me all at once, and those who lie in wait for me surrounded me along my paths.
My brothers have become strangers to me and have withdrawn far from me; even my friends have shown me no mercy.
My relatives no longer acknowledge me, and even those who know my name have forgotten me.
Even those close to me do not wish to see me, and they regard me as someone from another people.
I called my servants, but they ignored me.
I begged my wife and pleaded with her, but she mocked me. I appealed to the children of my servants and begged them for mercy.
They have rejected me forever; even when I rise, they slander me.
Even those who know me recoil from me; those whom I loved have risen against my life. 20 My skin is rotting together with my flesh, and the bones of my loins [?] me.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, my friends, for it is the hand of God that has struck me.
Why do you persecute me as God does? Have you not had enough of my flesh?
Who will write down my words and inscribe them in a book forever?
With an iron stylus and lead—or else let them carve it into rock.
But I know that he will not bring the house to an end [?]. The living one who will afterward stand upon the earth will heal me.
And while I am still on the earth, this too has come to me from God.
My skin will be changed. I myself know what my eye has seen, and not another. Everything has been fulfilled for me within my breast.
If you say, “What shall we say before him, and how shall we find the root of the matter against him?” then you too should fear disgrace.
For a scourge comes upon sinners, and then they will know where all the suffering that has overtaken them came from.
Then Zophar the Minaean answered
and said, “I did not expect you to speak like this, and you are no better than I am in understanding.
Listen to me, and I will tell you the wisdom of my instruction; the spirit of my understanding has answered me.
Do you know of anything like this before him, from your mother [?], or after you, or since the world was created?
The joy of sinners is a great slaughter, and the delight of the wicked is destruction.
And when he says, “I have finished; I am secure,” then he will perish forever, and those who know him will say, “Where is he?”
Even if his offering rises to heaven and his sacrifice reaches the clouds,
he flies away like an apparition and cannot be found. He appears like a dream of the night that cannot be recognized, and he resembles the morning.
The eye will no longer have its fill of seeing him, and his place will no longer recognize him.
The lowly will destroy his children, and his hands will fan the fire.
Pain will fill his bones, and his sickness will lie down in the earth.
For evil tastes sweet in his mouth, and he hides it beneath his tongue.
His food will turn over in his belly, and he will gather it in the middle of his throat.
It cannot help him, and the venom of a snake is beneath his lips.
The wealth he stores up through injustice will be wiped out, and the angel of death will drag him from his house.
Let him suck the venom of a snake, and let the tongue of a viper kill him.
He will not see the milk of his pastures; honey and oil will not flow, and he will not yoke again and again.
In vain and to no purpose he worked for his wealth, from which he will taste nothing. It is like something hard that cannot be chewed or swallowed.
For he laid waste many houses of the weak, and he plundered a dwelling and will not restore it.
No one will show him mercy on account of his wealth, and his desire will not prosper.
Nothing remains of his wealth, and therefore his prosperity will not endure.
When he says, “I have prevailed,” then he will become destitute, and every torment will come upon him and fill his belly.
The scourge of his wrath will increase, and what torments him will keep watch over him.
He will not escape the power of the spear, and a bronze bow will pierce him.
An arrow will pass through his flesh, and evil will stir in his soul, and something will come upon him that terrifies him.
Every darkness will await him, and a blazing fire will consume him, and his neighbor will mock him.
Heaven has revealed his wrongdoing, and the earth will not receive him.
Death will drag his house away forever, and the day of youth will come upon him.
This is the sinful man's portion from God, and the property he has acquired from his Creator.
Then Job spoke again and answered, saying:
“Listen to me and pay attention to my words, so that you do not say to me, ‘We are comforting him.’
“Be silent, and I will tell you, if there is anything for which you would laugh at me. It is not a human being who reproaches me, and how could one not become angry?
“Look at me and be astonished, and clap your hands.
“Even when I remember, I am troubled, and pain dwells in my flesh.”
Why do sinners live and act wickedly amid their wealth?
Even their offspring prosper before them, and their children fill their sight before them.
Their houses are full, and there is no one to frighten them; no punishment comes upon them from God.
Their cows are not barren, and their heifers do not miscarry; they come safely through giving birth.
They roam like sheep forever, and their children play, dance, and leap about.
Their parents rejoice at the sound of their songs.
They complete their days in prosperity and sleep in the bed of Sheol. 13 And they say to God, “Stay away from us! We do not want to see your ways.”

What can he do, that we should serve him? And what benefit is there for us in going to him? 15 Their prosperity is in their own hands, and he does not look at the deeds of sinners. 16 Yet the assembly of the wicked will perish, and their wickedness will overtake them; distress and punishment will come upon them.
They will become like straw before the wind and like dust carried away by a storm wind.

His children will not find his possessions, and he will take vengeance on them, and then he will know. 19 His [?] will not see when they torment his children, and God will not save them, because he does whatever he wishes.
And they will receive from the number of his months.
First of all, is it not God who teaches counsel and wisdom? And he takes vengeance on the murderer.
One person dies in the strength of his innocence, rejoicing in everything and prospering; his insides are full of fat, and his marrow flows.
Another dies in bitterness of soul, without eating anything good, or anything at all.
They all sleep together in the earth, and worms cover them.
And now I know that you have acted foolishly in rising against my life.
And if you say, “Where is the angel’s house, and where is the dwelling of reckless sinners?”
Ask those who travel the road; they find no knowledge of them.
For an evil day awaits sinners, and they will take him away on a day of evil and wrath.
Who [?] his way to his face, and who will repay him for what he himself has done?
They will carry him to the grave, and he will keep watch in his tomb.
The gravel of the stream will bury him, and all people will follow him; before him there are countless others.
Why, then, do you comfort me in vain? I have no rest with you.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite spoke again in reply and said:
First of all, is it not God who teaches counsel and wisdom?
What makes God glad when you purify your deeds? And what does he gain when you make your ways upright?
Will he take account of you and rebuke you? Will he come to argue his case with you?
First of all, is not your wickedness great, and are not your sins beyond counting?
You took a pledge from him for no reason and stripped the naked man of his clothing.
You did not even give water to the thirsty, and you withheld bread from the hungry. The man who sows possesses the land, and the favored person lives in it.
There are also some whose faces you admired, while you hated the poor and treated them unjustly on the earth.
You sent widows away naked and afflicted orphans.
Why have snares trapped you and a fierce attack terrified you?
Your light, too, has become darkness for you, and water has covered you while you sleep.
Is he not lofty and exalted? He does what he wishes and humbles the proud.
And you said, “What does the Mighty One know? Does he judge from above the darkness?
Clouds hide him, and he does not see. Does he walk around the vault of heaven?”
Will you keep to the ancient path that righteous men walked, who went up without being noticed, whose foundations were like a river in flood?
And those who say, “What will God do to us, and what will the ruler of all bring upon us?”—yet he filled their houses with blessing.
But the counsel of sinners is far from them.
The righteous saw them and laughed, and the innocent mocked them.
Their possessions perished, and fire consumed what remained of them.
Come now, be harsh if you can endure, and then your fruit will flourish.
Ask him about the word of your mouth, and put his word in your heart.
But if you repent and humble yourself before God, remove injustice from your heart.
He will plant you on a rock, and like a river stone he will [?].
The ruler of all will help you against your adversary and restore your purity to you like refined silver.
You will find favor before God and look toward heaven with joy.
He will hear you and give you what you pray to him for.
He will repay you for your righteousness and bring light to your paths.
For he humbled you; you will say, “He exalted the one who humbles himself.”
He will deliver the pure, and you will be saved through the purity of your hands.
Job spoke again and answered, saying:
“I know that my suffering comes from my own hand. He has made his hand heavy upon me and made me groan.
What is it that [?] does not know, so that I may find and reach [?] forever?
Let him tell me if there is anything I have done, and let him not silence my mouth when I make my complaint.
I also know that he will give me healing, and I have understood what he will give me.
Even if he comes with great power, he will not then act against me in his anger, for mercy and righteousness are with him.
And may he give me relief forever from my condemnation, for [?] beforehand.
And then he is not there, and then I do not discern what lies behind.
Then I go to the left and turn to the right, but there is nothing that I see.
And [?] knows my path, and he tested me like gold.
And he does not depart from his correction; I have kept his paths and have not transgressed.
I have not departed from his commandment, and I have hidden his word in my bosom.
Who will dispute with him about judgment? For he does whatever he wishes.
Because of this, I too was terrified on his account; after being rebuked, I thought about him.
Because of this, I trembled before his face; I think about him, and he terrifies me.
God has weakened my heart, and the one who rules over everything has terrified me.
How could I have known that darkness would come upon me, and that gloom would cover my face?
Why does God forget my appointed times?
Sinners crossed their boundaries and seized a shepherd along with his pasture.
They drove away an orphan’s donkey and took a widow’s ox.
They turned the weak away from the path of righteousness, and the meek of the earth gathered together.
They became like donkeys in the wilderness; they went out on my account and abandoned their work, and grain was their food from their youth.
Was it not fields that were not theirs that they harvested before the proper time? They forced those who lived alone to work in their vineyards; sinners oppressed them without wages and without food.
They denied clothing to many naked people and stripped them of the covering for their bodies.
Mist and the dew of the wilderness soak them, for they have no covering, and they shelter under rocks.
They snatched an orphan from the breast and caused pregnant women pain.
They oppressed the pregnant women and [?] them, and took away the hungry people’s sheaves.
They made the needy work and oppressed them, and they did not know justice.
They drove them from their houses and their towns, and made the children cry out all the more.
Why did he not rebuke these people while they were on earth? They neither knew nor saw the upright path, nor did they walk along its broad way.
Knowing their deeds, he delivered them into the power of darkness, and at night [?] like a thief.
The adulterer’s eye waits for darkness, and he says, “No one will see me,” and conceals himself from sight. 16. He digs through houses in the darkness; by day they hide and do not see the light.
When morning comes, it seems to them all like the shadow of death, for they know the terror that will come and expect to die.
He floats on the surface of the water; their portion on earth is cursed.
They see their plants withering on the earth, and they plundered the mortals who were there.

Then his sins will be remembered against him, and he will disappear like mist and dew. He will be repaid according to what he has done, and every wrongdoer will be shattered like rotten wood. 21. He did no good to the barren woman and showed no mercy to the woman who bore children.
He weakened the mighty in his anger, and when one rises, he has no confidence in his life.
If he becomes sick, he has no hope of living; instead, he falls ill.
He made many mourn through his appointment, and he withers like a mallow in the heat, like an ear of grain that falls by itself from its stalk.
If this is not so, who will call me a liar and make my words count for nothing?
Then Bildad the Shuhite spoke in reply and said:
From the beginning, does not majesty belong to him, who made everything in the heights?
Let no one think that there is any oversight concerning a robber. Whom has his calamity not reached?
How can a righteous person be pure before God? Who born of women can make himself clean?
Does not even the moon hide itself and fail to shine? Even the stars are not pure before him. How much less a mortal, a worm, a human being, a corpse!
Then Job spoke in reply and said:
Whom are you defending, and whom do you wish to help before him? Is it not the one whose strength is great and whose majesty inspires great awe?
Whom are you advising? Is it not the one who possesses wisdom? For whom are you pleading? Is it not the one whose strength is mighty?
To whom do you make known a message of the spirit? And whose spirit comes out of you?
Those who increase [?] oppressed me; the water beneath him and what is within it are not God.
Sheol lies exposed before him, and nothing is hidden from him.
He spread out heaven over nothing and suspended the earth over empty space.
He gathers the water in a cloud, and his cloud does not burst under its weight.
What is spread out for him [?] flies above his throne, and he places a cloud over it at all times.
He enclosed heaven by his command, and light and darkness pursue one another until the end.
He made the pillars of heaven firm, and they did not depart from his command; they tremble at his rebuke.
By his strength he quieted the sea, and by his rebuke he struck the sea monster.
The gates of Sheol trembled before him, and by his rebuke he killed the rebellious serpent.
Look, this is only a part of his ways, and we shall hear his remaining words. Who knows the sound of his thunder when he acts?
Job continued again and said:
As God lives, who has judged me this way, and as the ruler of all lives, who has embittered my soul!
As long as my life remains, and the spirit of God still enables me to speak, my mouth will not speak injustice, and my soul will not learn sin.
I would rather [?] than declare you righteous, unless I die, for I will not abandon it throughout my life.
As long as I practice righteousness, it will not fail, for I am not aware of having done evil.
But let my enemies be like the downfall of sinners, and those who rise against me like the death of the lawless.
Why does a sinner remain alive, hoping to live? Will someone who has not trusted in God be saved?
Will he hear his prayer? And if trouble comes, will he find favor with him?
And if he calls on him, will he give to him and answer him?
But I will tell you what is in God's hand, and I will not lie about what is with the Almighty.
You all know that evil comes upon the wicked.
This is the sinful man's portion from God, and the wealth of the mighty will come to him from the Almighty.
Even if his children become numerous, they will be destined for destruction; and even if they grow strong, they will beg.
And no one will care for their widows.
Even if he gathers silver like dirt and piles up gold like clay,
the righteous will consume it all, and the upright will obtain his wealth.
His house will become like dust and like something eaten by moths.
The rich man lies down, and there is no one to wake him. He opens his eyes and is astonished.
Suffering will surround him like water, and a whirlwind will carry him away.
A scorching wind will seize him, and he will pass away; it will sweep him from his dwelling.
What he does not expect will come upon him and will not spare him. He will not escape from its hand, and he will pass away.
He will clap his hands over me and sweep him out of his house.
There is a place from which silver comes, and there is a place where they refine gold.
Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is hewn out like stone.
He has set a limit to darkness, and he searches out everything: the stone of darkness and the shadow of death.
Like a torrent breaking through the ground, those who forget the path of righteousness have grown weak in their sins.
Grain comes from the earth, but underneath he overturns it with fire.
There is a place of sapphire stones, and its gold is like dust.
There is a path that no bird has seen and that the eagle's eye has not observed.
The offspring of the proud have not walked on it, and no lion has passed through it.
He raised his hand against the flint and destroyed the mountains from their foundations and their roots.
He split open the springs of rivers, and my eye saw every precious thing.
He split open the depths of rivers and revealed his power in the light.
Where was wisdom found, and where is the dwelling place of wisdom?
No mortal knows its path, and it is not found among human beings.
The deep said, “It is not with me,” and the sea said, “It does not dwell with me.”
Nothing equal to it has been found, and silver is not suitable in exchange for it.
It cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir, or with precious onyx and sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can gold vessels serve as its price.
Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning beside it. Draw wisdom from [?] according to your strength. 19. The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, and it cannot be bought with pure gold.
Where was wisdom found, and where is the dwelling place of understanding?
For it has been forgotten by all people and is hidden even from the birds of the sky.
Death and Sheol said, “We have heard its voice.”
God has made its face beautiful, and he himself knows its dwelling place.
He sees everything in heaven and knows everything on earth.
He himself made the winds by weight and the water by measure.
When he created them in this way, knowing it, he counted it; when he made a rule for the rain, and on the path [?] the voice.
Then he saw it and counted it, prepared it, honored it, and drew it forth.
He said to humanity, “Look, the fear of God is wisdom, and turning away from every evil is understanding.”
Job spoke again and said:
“Who will bring me back to the days of my former months, when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone above my head, and when I walked by his light through darkness,
when I lived amid every blessing, and when God visited my house,
when my possessions were abundant and my servants were around me,
When oil flowed along my paths, and when milk poured through my mountains.
when I went forth in the splendor of my city and set my seat in the square?
Young men saw me and hid from me, and all the elders stood waiting for me.
The powerful fell silent and did not speak; they closed their mouths with their hands.
Those who heard me called me blessed, and their tongues clung to their throats.
The ear that heard me called me blessed, and the eye that saw me [?].
For I rescued the poor from the hand of the one who oppressed him, and I helped the orphan who had no helper.
And the dying man followed me, and the widow's mouth blessed me.
I clothed myself in righteousness, put on uprightness like a cloak, and crowned myself with justice.
I was eyes for the blind and feet for the crippled.
I was a father to the poor, and I sought justice for the one who did not know it.
I broke the fangs of the oppressors and rescued from between their teeth what they had seized.
I thought, 'I will grow old and become forgetful, and keep my trunk alive for years like a tall palm shoot, and multiply my days like the sand.'
Water will be poured over my roots, and dew will descend upon my harvest.
My glory remains fresh with me, and I walk with my bow in my hand.
They waited for me and listened to me, and they kept silent at my counsel.
They added no further word after my words, and they rejoiced when I spoke to them.
Like thirsty land that waits for rain, so they waited for my words.
They did not believe it when I laughed with them, and the light of my face did not fade.
I sought out their way and sat judging them. I sat alone like a king, and when they mourned, they took comfort in me.
But now the lowly laugh at me. Today they alone admonish me—those whose fathers I despised and did not consider equal even to the dogs of my pasture.
What use is the strength of their hands to me? Let death come upon them.
They feed [?] because of hunger, licking [?], those who flee from the hand of the wilderness, yesterday in toil and misery.
They howl and beg and [?], living in [?], needy and violent and deprived of every good thing. They chew tree roots because of their great hunger.
Robbers rose against me, whose houses are in the hollows of rocks.
They warm themselves among the [?] and hide in the grass of the wilderness.
Foolish offspring, with no name, for they are lost from the earth, and wisdom has disappeared from the earth.
Now I have become their lyre, and I am their taunt.
They recoil from me and keep their distance, and they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
The mighty one opened his quiver and killed me, and let loose a bridle against my face.
He rose against me with a powerful right hand, spread his feet over me, and made a road of death against me.
He erased my tracks, stripped me of my clothes, and pierced me with his arrows.
He made me whatever he wished, and I despair in pain.
Adversaries continually assail me; my soul wastes away within me and is worn down, and my life has passed like a cloud that disperses.
And now my soul is poured out within me, and anguish has overwhelmed me.
All night my bones burn, and my sinews waste away.
With great force they twisted my clothing, and the opening of my garment choked me, and he [?] a claw into my neck.
They regarded me as a heap of earth, and dust became my portion.
I cried out to you, but you did not hear me; though I stood there, he paid me no attention. Those without mercy attacked me, and the hand that struck me grew stronger.
He abandoned me to suffering and removed me far from my life.
I know that [?] death will crush me, and the earth is the dwelling place of everyone who has died.
If I wanted to eat alone and did not let another share, let another do the same to me.
I weep for every afflicted person, and I shed tears when I see someone suffering.
I held firmly to what is good, but now evil days have overtaken me. I hoped for light, but darkness came upon me.
My belly boils and does not rest, and days of anguish have overtaken me.
I went about in distress, with no one to give me relief. I sinned and stood among many people, and they cried out.
I became a brother to ostriches and a companion to birds.
My skin [?] down my back; I have been burned, and my bones have been scorched.
My pain became my lyre, and my tears became my song.
I set a rule for my eyes, and I did not look at a virgin.
Furthermore, I did not eat God's portion or the inheritance of the Mighty One from on high.
Woe to the death of the wicked, and rejection to those who commit sin!
Does he not see my path and count all my steps?
If I walked with mockers, and if my foot strayed from his path,
I stood on an honest scale, and God knows my innocence.
My foot strayed from his path; and if my heart followed my eyes, and if I reached with my hands for [?], let another person eat what I have sown.
Let me be without roots upon the earth. And if my heart followed another man's wife, and if I watched the door of her house,
let my wife serve another man, and let my children be humbled by the stroke of his overwhelming wrath.
For defiling another man's wife is a fire that burns through every part; wherever it enters, it destroys from the roots.
And if I despised the claim of my male slave or my female slave when they brought a complaint against me,
what will I say to God if he calls me to account? And if there is someone who presses charges against me, shall I argue before him?
Were they not made just as I was made in my mother's womb, and did we not dwell in that womb?
Formerly I brought to completion the work I intended, and I did not make a widow's eyes fail.
If I ever ate my food alone and did not give any of it to an orphan—
I cared for him from his youth like his father, and I brought him up from his mother's womb, from the day he was born.
And if I saw someone naked and did not clothe him while he was dying from the cold.
The destitute blessed me, and their backs were warmed by the wool of my sheep.
If I raised my hand against an orphan, trusting that I had much support, let my arm be severed from my shoulder, and let my hand be broken off at the elbow.
For dread of God seized me, and there is no escape from his grasp.
And if I buried my gold in the earth, and if I trusted in gems of great value—
And if I rejoiced in my great wealth, and if I laid my hand on possessions beyond counting—
Does he not see the sun, which shines and fades, and the moon weeping because she cannot govern herself?
And no one secretly led my heart astray. And if I put my hand over my mouth, and if I heard and remained silent—
Let this also be a great sin against me, if I lied before God Most High.
And if I rejoiced at the downfall of my enemies, and if I said in my heart, “Good!”—
Let my ear hear evil, and let an evil name ring out among my people.
Those living with me said, “Who would give us his flesh to eat?” though I was very merciful to them.
No traveler spent the night outside, and my house was open to everyone passing through. If I sinned and concealed it, let my guilt be great.
And I was ashamed before many people to contend with them; and if a poor man went out of my door naked—

Who would give me someone to hear me? And if I did not fear the hand of God, and if I had a written charge from the one who calls me to account, I would carry it on my shoulders and read it before many people.
I would spread it out and return it, taking nothing from the one who calls me to account.
And if I made the earth cry out, and if its furrows wept—
And if I ate my food [?] without payment, and if I drove away the owner of the land and grieved his soul—
Let weeds grow for me instead of wheat, and let thorns grow for me instead of barley. And Job stopped speaking.
These three friends of his fell silent and no longer answered Job, because Job was righteous in his own eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the people of Aram, from the land of Uz, became angry. He was very angry with Job because Job declared himself righteous before God.
He was also very angry with Job's three friends, because they could not give Job an answer that matched what he had said, yet they treated him as a sinner.
Elihu waited for them to answer Job, because they were older than he was.
When Elihu saw that there were no words in the mouths of these three men, his anger burned against them.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, “I am young in years, while you are elders and learned men. Therefore I remained silent, afraid to tell you what I think.”

And I said, “But it is not years that give understanding, nor do many seasons make wisdom known. 8. Rather, it is the spirit upon a mortal, and the spirit of the one who rules everything, that teaches.”
Those who have lived many seasons are not necessarily wise, nor do elders necessarily understand justice.
But listen to me. I will tell you what I know. Pay attention to my words.
And I will make it known to you as you listen to me, until you find something to say.
Look, there was no one among you who rebuked Job or answered [?] concerning what he said, so that you should not say, “We have found wisdom from God, and we have surpassed him.”
They allowed the man to speak words like these.
You were afraid and gave no answer, and speech failed from your mouths.
I waited for you, but you did not speak, because you remained silent and did not answer.
When Elihu spoke, he answered and said, “Listen again to what I tell you.”
I am full of words [?], and the spirit within my belly is killing me.
My belly is tied up like a wineskin, and my [?] seethes, like a coppersmith’s burst bellows.
I will speak so that I may breathe freely, and I will open my lips.
For I will not stand in fear of a human being or show favor to a mortal.
I do not know how to show partiality, even if there is someone who stands in fear of people.
But listen to my voice, Job, and pay attention to my words.
Look, I have opened my mouth, and my tongue has spoken.
My heart thinks purely, and my lips speak wisdom and offer pure counsel.
God created me, and the spirit of the one who rules everything teaches me.
If you can answer me about this matter, bear with me. I will speak to you, and you too must answer me.
You were formed from dust, just like me, and from it we were both drawn.
I will not distress you. Do not be anxious about me, and my hand will not weigh heavily upon you.
But I will tell you your wrongdoing. I have heard your words and your wrongdoing as well.
Listen to the sound of my words, for you said, “I am pure and have done no wrong. I am righteous and have committed no sin.”
I gave him something to say, and he treated me as an enemy.
“He put my feet in the stocks and fixed all my paths.”
How can you say, “I am righteous, and he does not hear my voice”? He is eternal and above mortals.
How can you say, “He does not hear all my righteousness”?
For God speaks once through the prophets, and a second time in a dream, or else in a message at night.
And he brings great terror upon a person while he sleeps on his bed.
Then he opens a person's heart so that the person sees terror and is afraid.
And he turns a person away from his sin and saves his body from falling.
He spares his soul from death, so that he does not fall into destruction.
Again, he disciplines him with sickness on his bed, and all his bones ache.
He cannot taste any food made from grain, yet his soul longs to eat grain.
Until his flesh wastes away and his bones appear bare.
His soul draws close to death, and his life to Sheol.

Even if there are a thousand angels of death, not one of them will kill him if he resolves in his heart to return to God, to declare a person's sin to him and show him his error, so that he guards himself against falling into death.
He renews his soul like a coating of plaster, so that his bones become full of marrow.
He makes his flesh tender like a child's flesh and makes him stronger than other people.
When he prays to God, God accepts him. He comes before him with a pure face, speaking, and God repays a person for his righteousness.
Then the person blames himself and says, “What have I done? What has happened to me because of my error is less than I deserve.
He has saved my soul from going into decay, so that my life may see light.”
Look, the Mighty One does all this, and his ways toward a person are three.
But he saved my soul from death, so that my life might be praised in the light.
And listen to me. If you have something to say, speak; tell me, for I desire that you be vindicated.
But if you have something to say, speak; tell me, for I desire that you be vindicated.
But if not, listen to me and be silent; I will teach you wisdom.
Elihu spoke again and said:
“Listen to me, you wise people, and pay close attention to me, you who have understanding.
For the ear distinguishes words, and the palate tastes food.
Let us choose what is right for ourselves, and let us determine among ourselves what is better.
For Job said, ‘I am righteous, but my judgment has brought condemnation upon me, and I suffer unjustly, though I am without guilt.’
Who is a person like Job, who drinks endurance like water?
He has not sinned or gone astray at all; he has not associated with evildoers or walked with sinners.
And he said, ‘They will not help a person in his eagerness before God.’
Now listen to me, you who are wise in heart. Do not wish to sin before God, and do not oppress the righteous before the one who rules everything.
He repays every person according to his deeds and causes each person to receive according to his ways.
Do you make God out to be an oppressor, and the ruler of everything to be one who perverts justice—he who created the earth?
Who is it who made what is beneath heaven and everything in it?
If he wished, he could exert his power and take back the spirit that comes from him.
Then all flesh would die together, every mortal, and return to the earth from which it was created.
But if not, accept correction and listen to these words, and speak with your own throat.
He who hates injustice and destroys the wicked is righteous forever.
Cursed is the one who says to a king, ‘You have sinned,’ and calls messengers evil.
He shows no partiality to the honored, does not recognize the prestige of the mighty, and is not intimidated by their presence.
The one who cries out finds only futility; he does not listen to people and has done evil to the poor.
He himself sees people's deeds, and nothing is hidden from him.
There is no place where evildoers can hide, for they cannot escape from God, who sees everything.
He knows things that cannot be traced, glorious and wonderful things beyond counting.
He knows their deeds, brings night upon them, and afflicts them.
He destroys sinners, but the righteous are before him.
Those who have transgressed God's law do not recognize his judgment: he brings the cries of the needy back upon them and hears the outcry of the poor.
He gives them rest, and who can condemn? He hides his face, and no one can see him, whether a nation or an individual alike.
God makes a deceitful man king because of the wickedness of the people, one who says to the Mighty One, ‘I have taken, and I have nothing to hold.’
‘I myself will see; you too, show me if I have done wrong or spoken falsely, so that I do not say it again.’
Did I take it from you, that you should drive me away? For you choose, not I.
If you know anything, tell me, for those who are wise in heart speak this way, and a wise man listens to my words.
But Job does not speak like a wise man, and his speech is not that of a learned man.
But learn, Job, and no longer respond like fools,
so that you do not add folly to your sins, and speaking many words before God does not become an offense for you.
Elihu answered and said:
What do you say in your own defense? And who are you to say, ‘I am righteous before God’?
And you say, “What will I accomplish if I sin?”
I will answer you and your three friends.
Look at the sky and see; understand how far the clouds are above you.
If you sin, what do you do to him? Even if your offenses are many, what can you do to him?
If you are righteous, what have you given him? What has he received from you?
Your sin affects a person like yourself, and your righteousness affects a fellow human being.
Because of the multitude of oppressors, they groan and cry out because of the power of the many.
But no one says, “Where is God, who made me, who does not command sleep at night, who makes me better than the animals of the earth and the birds of the sky?”
There they cry out, but he does not hear them because of the pride of the wicked.
For God does not wish to look upon evil, because he who rules everything is wise.
He does not listen to those who do wrong. Present your case before him, then, if you can praise him as he is.
And now, because no one knows the time of his anger, and he does not take account of his great sin. 15 But Job speaks in vain and opens his mouth; without knowledge he multiplies his words.
Then Elihu spoke again and said:
“Bear with me a little longer, and I will teach you, for I still have something to say.
I will bring back my words from afar, and I will declare my deeds righteous.
My words are true, not false, and God does not listen to injustice.
But know that God does not abandon the innocent; he is mighty and strong.
He does not preserve the life of a sinful heart, but he gives justice to the poor.
He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous. He looks after the righteous and seats them on thrones with kings; he seats them on high in their triumph, and they are honored.
Even those whose hands are bound with chains are held by the cord of poverty.
He tells them about their deeds and their offenses, because they are many.
But he hears the righteous and tells them to turn back from their sins.
If they listen and serve him, they will finish their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.
But he does not hear sinners or save them, because they do not wish to look to God, and when he rebukes them, they do not listen.
The hypocrites set their hearts on anger, and they cry out when he humiliates them.
Their souls perish in their youth, and angels bring their lives to an end.
For they afflicted the poor and needy and turned aside the [?] of the innocent.
They mocked you with the mouths of your enemies. An abyss pours out beneath you, and your table descends, full and rich.”
His wrath comes upon the destitute who have taken counsel to [?]; and do not forget your former sin.
Do not let mockery or the plea of the needy in their distress lead you astray.
But guard yourself and do good, and do not do evil; through this you will be saved from poverty.
Look, the Mighty One prevails by his strength, and who can contend with him?
Who can question his deeds, and who can say to him, “What have you done?”
And remember how great his work is.
Men who judged and those who were judged—every person considers for himself that sinners are dead.
Look, he is mighty and great; the number of his ways cannot be seen or known.
The drops of rain that pour from within a cloud cannot be counted.
He orders what has grown old and spreads a cloud over mortals, and rain pours down without number.
He knows the breadth of the clouds according to the extent of his shade.
Look, he spreads his knowledge over it and covers the waves of the sea.
For through them he judges the nations and gives the unborn child its food.
And for the little one he covers the light, and he commands it [?].
