His friend tells about him, about what befell him because of his wrongdoing.
Because of this my heart trembled and fell from its place.
Listen, then, to the sound of the scourge of God's wrath and to the word that comes from his mouth.
He sends it beneath all the heavens, and his light over the ends of the earth.
After it he rebukes with a voice and thunders with the voice of his wrath; he has mercy on them when he hears their voice.

He thunders with a terrifying roar and directs the animals, each at its proper time, and knows when they lie down. In all this, do not let your heart be startled, and do not let your heart be displaced from its flesh. He has done great things that we do not know.
He commands snow to fall upon the earth, and the winter rain falls by his power.
He restrains everyone's hands so that every human being may know his labor.
The wild animals go beneath shelter and rest in their lairs.
Sickness comes upon them from hunger, and they grow cold in their dwellings.
From a mighty wind comes [?], and he divides the water as he wishes.

He hides the chosen ones in a cloud and scatters the cloud with his light. He turns it in its circuit; his purpose is one in his work, in everything he has commanded them, according to the order that comes from him upon the earth.
Whether for what is in the wilderness, or for what is on the earth, or for what is in goodness, he reaches it.
Listen to this, Job; accept correction and stand in the power of God.
We know that God has ordered his works and made light out of darkness.
Do you know the dividing of the clouds, the terrible downfall of sinners?
But your clothes are warm; be silent, then, upon the earth.
Can you strengthen your struggle with him from the south? His appearance is awesome to many.
Tell me why, and what we should say to him. Let us be silent, then, and you too must not speak much.
Does he have a book and a scribe, so that I should remain silent when a man stands before me?
Not everyone can perceive the light; it is light within [?], like that which comes from him in the clouds [?].
Is there such great glory and honor with the one who rules everything?
We find no other like him in strength, who judges justly and does not wish to listen to him.
Yet human beings fear him, and those who are wise at heart fear him.
And afterward Elihu stopped [?].
Then the Lord questioned Job in a cloud and a storm.
He said, “Who is the man who hides counsel from me and stores up words in his heart, concealing them even from me?
Gird your waist like a man. I will question you, and you must answer me.
Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundations? Tell me, if you are wise.
Who determined its measurements, if you know? And who stretched measuring cords over it?
On what are its rings suspended, and who established its corners?
When the stars were created, all my angels praised me with a loud voice.
I enclosed the sea with gates when it came out of its mother’s womb.
I made clouds its clothing and wrapped it in mist.
I set a boundary for it and placed bars and gates within it.
I said to it, ‘Come this far, and do not cross your boundary; instead, let your waves roll within you.’
Was the light of dawn put in order by you, and did the morning star learn its command?
It turns at the edges of the earth to clear the sinners out of it.
Did you take dust from the earth, fashion a living being, and make it speak upon the earth?
Did you take their light away from sinners and shatter the arms of the proud?
Have you reached the seabed or walked along the paths of the deep?
Do the gates of death open to you because of your majesty, and do the gatekeepers of Sheol tremble when they see you?
Do you know the breadth of what lies beneath heaven? Tell me how great it is.
And where is the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness?
Send me, then, to their borders.
If you know their way, then surely you know, since you were born at that time and the number of your years is great.
Have you reached the storehouse of hail, and have you seen where the snow is stored?
Is it kept for you for the time of your enemy, for the day of battle and slaughter?
Where does frost come from, and where does the south wind turn beneath the sky?
Who strengthens the mighty rain along the paths of the wilderness?
So that it rains on a wilderness land, where there are no people and no human being lives;
And so that it waters places where there are no trees and no one lives, making grass sprout in the wilderness.
Who is the father of the rain, and who gives birth to the blossoms of dew?
From whose womb does ice come out, and who gives birth to the frost in heaven so that it descends?
The waters hide among stones and flow like water. And who has humbled the [?] of sinners?
Do you know the bonds of the many, and have you held back the river? Do you release winter each year and bring summer afterward at its appointed time?
Do you know the course of heaven, or what happens together beneath heaven?
Can you restrain the Pleiades so that they do not move? Have you seen the path of Aldebaran and its rising? 34. Do you know the time of the Great Bear and its revolution?
Do you call the clouds with your voice, and does abundant water answer you with trembling?
Do you send lightning on its way, and does it say to you, “What is it?”
Who gave animals wisdom so that they [?], and [?] instruction?
Who counted the clouds in his wisdom and established the sky above the earth?
It was poured out upon the earth, and they made it stick together like rock.
Have you hunted prey for lions, and do you satisfy the hunger of dragons?
They enter their dens, remain among the trees, and lie in wait.
Who prepares food for the ravens when their young cry out to God and search for something to eat?
Do you know the time when the deer gives birth, and have you watched it during labor?
Have you counted its months until it gives birth, and have you freed them from pain?
Have you fed its young without fear, and do you relieve their pain?
Their young break free, grow, and reproduce. They go away and do not return to them.
Who set the wild donkey free, and who untied its bonds?
And he made the wilderness his dwelling place, and the salt land his home.
He laughs at the crowds of people and does not hear the voice of the one who drives him.
He goes into the wilderness to graze and searches for green vegetation.
Will the wild ox be willing to serve you and spend the night in your house?
Will you bind him to a post and put a yoke on his neck, so that he plows the furrows of your fields for you?
Will you rely on him because his strength is great and leave your work to him?
Will you trust him to bring in your harvest for you and deliver your grain?
The ostrich that [?] and sits, after she has conceived, wants to eat and hides her eggs in the ground.
She lays her young in the earth, leaves them where she gave birth, and goes among the wild animals.
She neglects her young and [?] there. She labors and suffers in vain, yet she has no fear.
For God gave her wisdom and allotted her understanding and wisdom.
And in her season she cries out and rises high, and she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Did you give the horse its strength and clothe its neck with majesty?
Have you made it charge into battle with weapons of war?
With the majesty of its shoulders, as it runs, it digs deep into the ground with its feet and advances into the open country with its strength.
It laughs at the [?] who takes vengeance on it and does not turn back from the arrow. 22. Against it the bow, the sword, and the spear press hard.
In its fury it ravages the earth and cannot be trusted until the horn is blown.
When the horn is blown, it says, “Aha!” from far away, and it smells the battle.
Is it by your wisdom that the hawk stands with its wings spread and remains motionless, turned toward the south?
Is it at your command that the eagle rises, and that the vulture spends the night sheltering its young?
It dwells in the caves of the rocks and hides its young there.
After settling them there, they run toward blood, and wherever there is a carcass, they arrive at once.
And the Lord answered Job and said to him:
Is it with your equal that you are disputing, that you argue while God rebukes you?
And Job answered the Lord and said to him:
What can I say in reply while you teach me? And who am I to dispute with God when I hear this? What answer can I give except to put my hand over my mouth?
I have spoken once, and I will not speak again now.
And again God answered Job from the cloud and said to him:
But gird your waist like a man. I will question you, and you must answer me.
Otherwise, leave my judgment alone. Do you think someone else judges you, rather than that you might display your righteousness?
Is your arm like God's, and is your voice like thunder?
Clothe yourself, then, with power from on high, and array yourself in honor and glory.
Send out the angels of death, and humiliate your enemy.
Destroy the proud, and at that very moment bury the wicked. Make them decay together in the ground outside.
Fill their faces with shame, and hide them in the ground outside.
And I too will acknowledge that your right hand is able to save.
Look, the beast beside you grazes on grass like cattle.
And look, his power is in his loins, and his strength is in the navel of his belly.
It holds its back (its tail) erect like a cypress tree, and its sinews are intertwined.
The bones of its ribs are bronze, and the bones of its back are cast iron.
This is the first of God's works, and when it was made, his angels laughed at it.
It went into a high mountain and [?] a place for its animals in the cold.
It lies beneath every tree, among papyrus, sedges, and reeds.
The sycamore tree and the branches of the poplar shade it.
Even if abundant water comes, it does not alarm it. It is confident that it can draw the Jordan into its mouth.
It receives it with its eye, draws it in, and guards its nose.
Can you catch the crocodile with a hook and put a bridle in its nose?
Can you fasten a ring in its lip and pierce its nose with a thorn?
Will it entreat you, pleading and speaking gently to you?
Will it make a covenant with you, so that you can take it to remain with you as your slave forever?
Can you tie it up like a little bird and play with it like a bird?
The nations also plead with it, and the people of Phoenicia receive it.
Even if all the birds gather together, they cannot carry away a single piece of skin from its back, nor can fishermen carry its head in boats.

Lay your hand on him to touch him; remember how he fought against your body, and do not do it again. 33 You have also seen his case, yet you were not afraid or astonished, for you prepared him for me.
Who is it that opposes me?
And who can contend with me and live? Everything under heaven is mine.
He will not be silent about him, and with a word of power he will show mercy to one like him.
Who can strip away the covering of his face? And who can enter the folds of his armor?
And who can open the doors before his face? Terror surrounds his teeth.
His inward parts are beasts of iron, and his fastening is like solid rock.
Each is joined to the next, and not even air can pass between them.
Each fits against its neighbor; they cling together and cannot be separated.
His sneezing flashes with light, and his eyes are like the morning star.
Burning torches come out of his mouth, and they scatter glowing coals.
Smoke comes out of his nostrils, like a furnace burning with fiery coals.
His breath is burning coal, and flame comes out of his mouth. 13 Strength dwells in his neck, and death waits before him for anyone who sees him.
The flesh of his body is firmly joined; even if they melt stone over him, he does not move.
His heart is hard as rock, and he stands like a young man.
Even when he turns around, all the wild animals, the livestock, and everything that moves on the earth tremble.
Even if craftsmen assail him, there is nothing they can do to him.
A spear and a coat of iron are like grass before him, and iron is like rotten wood.
An iron bow cannot pierce him, and stones are like grass. He regards a splitting rod as [?], and he spreads himself over a great stone.
His bed is a great pillar, and all the gold of the sea is to him like dust beyond counting.
He makes Sheol boil like a pot, and he regards the sea as ointment.
The frost of Sheol is like salt, and he has made Sheol a place to walk.
There is nothing like him on the earth, and when he was created, his angels laughed at him.
He sees everything that is high, and he is king over everything in heaven.
Then Job answered the Lord and said:
“I know full well that you can do everything; everything is possible for you, and nothing is beyond your power.”
Who is it who hides counsel from you and [?] a word in his heart, and thinks he can conceal it from [?]? And who will tell me what I do not know—great wonders that I have not seen?
Hear me, and I will speak to you, my Lord. I will ask you, and you teach me.
Before, I had heard of you with my ears, but now I have seen you with my eyes.
But because I went astray, I have humbled myself. I know that I myself am earth and dust.

After the Lord had spoken these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You and your two friends have sinned, because you have not spoken what is right before me as my servant Job has—not even once.

Now take seven bulls and seven sheep, and go to my servant Job. Let him offer a sacrifice, and let my servant Job pray for you. I will accept him on your behalf. If it were not for him, I would have killed you, because you have not spoken rightly about my servant Job.”
Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Minaean went and did as the Lord had commanded them, and the Lord forgave their sins for Job’s sake.

The Lord restored Job to health, and Job prayed for his friends, and he forgave their sins. The Lord gave Job all his possessions, twice as much as all he had possessed before, and doubled them for him.

All his brothers and sisters heard what had happened to him, and all who had known him before came to him. They ate and drank with him, cheered him, and marveled at all that the Lord had brought upon him. He gave each of them a pair of oxen, and gold and silver weighing four didrachms.

The Lord blessed Job in his later life more than before. His livestock numbered fourteen thousand, his sheep six thousand, his pairs of oxen one thousand, his female donkeys one thousand, and his camels one thousand.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
He named the first Day (Sun), the second Cassia, and the third Amalthea’s Horn.
And no women as beautiful as Job’s daughters were found beneath heaven, and their father gave them their inheritance along with their brothers.

Job lived for one hundred and seventy years after his affliction. His entire life was two hundred and forty-eight years, and he saw his children and his children’s children, down to the fourth generation.
Job died old, having completed his days.
It is written that he will rise again with those whom God raises.
And this is its translation from the Syriac book: the land where he lived was Uz, on the border of Edom in Arabia.
They called him Jobab. The man married an Arabian woman, and she bore him a son named Ennon. This Job’s father was Zerah, and his mother was Bosorrah. He was the fifth generation from Abraham.
These are the kings who reigned in Edom.
The first to rule in the region was Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

After Balak came Jobab, whose name was Job; and after him came Husham, who ruled the land of Teman, 24; and after him came Hadad son of Bedad, who killed the Midianites in the plain of Moab. The name of his city was Getham.
His friends who came to him were Eliphaz, a descendant of Esau and king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans.
